Hi @mattlewis92, thanks for the contributions!

I had to think about it for a second from a strictness perspective, but this seems like a good fix. In general we should rely on TypeScript to catch strictness issues (e.g. reading a property from a type that doesn't have it). Otherwise the evaluator should indeed follow JS behavior and return `undefined` - as long as TypeScript is otherwise cool with the property access (e.g. the property is optional allows `undefined` as a value). So this change looks good!

issue_context.title: ivy providers don't work with config object passed to forRoot
issue_context.body:
# 🐞 bug report ### Affected Package @angular/compiler ### Is this a regression? No, it's ivy only ### Description I tried out ivy on my project and the only error I got was ``` ERROR in Invalid map access: [] dot eventTitleFormatter ``` The issue is caused by this line: https://github.com/mattlewis92/angular-calendar/blob/try-ivy/projects/angular-calendar/src/modules/calendar.module.ts#L56 Where I pass a config object of providers ``` export class CalendarModule { static forRoot( dateAdapter: Provider, config: CalendarModuleConfig = {} ): ModuleWithProviders { return { ngModule: CalendarModule, providers: [ dateAdapter, config.eventTitleFormatter || CalendarEventTitleFormatter, config.dateFormatter || CalendarDateFormatter, config.utils || CalendarUtils ] }; } } ``` Removing it and the app compiled and everything else worked great, very impressive to see the commitment to backwards compatibility 🎉 ## 🔬 Minimal Reproduction Checkout this branch: https://github.com/mattlewis92/angular-calendar/tree/try-ivy ``` npm i npm start ``` and you'll see the error ## 🔥 Exception or Error 

ERROR in Invalid map access: [] dot eventTitleFormatter
## 🌍 Your Environment **Angular Version:** 

Angular CLI: 8.0.0
Node: 12.1.0
OS: darwin x64
Angular: 8.0.0
... animations, cdk, cli, common, compiler, compiler-cli, core

comments: Could you test with `next` packages? That error should no longer occur as of #30247.

Nice, thanks for the fast reply! `next` is currently set to `8.0.0` so I can't try it, but if it was merged 13 days ago wouldn't it have been included in `8.0.0` as there's been several releases cut since then?

`next` not being available as 8.1.x seems to be an oversight. Since the release of 8.0.0-rc.0 about a month ago, the master branch has already been designated for 8.1.x development. Since work on Ivy is typically only merged to master, the patch branch has been missing out on the latest fixes.

Please see https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/29564#issuecomment-496809489 for an alternative approach on how to run from `master`.

Ah gotcha, makes sense. I tried the version from the cli builds on github and I'm getting the same error. I looked at the source and that patch is 100% in my node_modules: You can play with it yourself here to verify: https://github.com/mattlewis92/angular-calendar/tree/try-ivy Thanks!

Ah thanks, that helps a lot. I misjudged the actual problem here, which is that it is currently not allowed to read a non-existent property from an object. Since that has well-defined behavior in JavaScript, we should just evaluate it as `undefined`.

When replacing the `throw new Error(...)` with simply returning `undefined` the app does compile, with heaps of template type errors. There's #30675 to fix some, but others look legit ;) The new template type checking should be more accurate, but if you spot false positives please let us know.

If you feel like it, you could open a PR with a fix for the static evalutor. If you need help with that or are not interested, let me know :)

Sure, I'd be happy to contribute! Could do with some pointers for writing a failing test case 😄 I can base it off your changes in https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/30247/files but I'm not really sure what to put in `evaluate` and what assertions to run.

Nice! For a test case, how about declaring a variable that is initialized to an object literal (that would be the first arg to `evaluate`) and then reading a non-existent property from that variable in the second arg. The outcome is expected to be `undefined`.

You can run that specific testsuite using `yarn test-ivy-aot packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/partual_evaluator/test`, optionally with `--config=debug` to be able to attach a debugger from `chrome://inspect`.
Sweet, thanks for the help, here you go: https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/30738

review_comments:
Hi Matt,

Thanks for contributing a fix!

Quick question: does it make sense to add one more test case with extra nesting level, like this:

```
evaluate('const obj: any = {}', 'obj.bar.baz')
```

I guess returning `undefined` makes sense with `obj.bar` expression, but I'm wondering if we still need to throw an error while evaluating `obj.bar.baz`?

Thank you.

cc @JoostK @alxhub

@AndrewKushnir we should probably add a test for that, although its outcome is not affected by this PR. When evaluating the property access `baz`, its LHS will evaluate to `undefined` and ngtsc's `accessHelper` will return a `DynamicValue`:

https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/f3444b8156b77a7690f335ee9d5ca3ebc1afa3e7/packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/partial_evaluator/src/interpreter.ts#L373

We would end up in the same situation if the test code was `const obj: any = { bar: undefined }`, hence this PR does not affect that particular scenario.

In general, I do think we should update the static evaluator to *never* throw an error, as doing so prevents from being able to accurately tell where the problem is. We may want to introduce a `DynamicValue` that represents an error condition instead, so that we can properly report errors.
Thanks for additional info @JoostK, that makes sense. I don't want to delay this PR, so I think we can add extra tests later if needed. Thank you.
